idea-plugin.name: Keymap Manager
idea-plugin.description:
Keymap Manager — a macOS-focused keymap manager. It finds where your JetBrains keymap collides with macOS or with itself, explains what's actually happening, and lets you fix any bound shortcut in place: rebind, remove, or revert to the parent binding — one action, several at once, or a whole category, inherited bindings included. It also manages keymaps (activate, duplicate, rename, delete, import/export as XML) and bundles MacBook Pro DE, a ready-made keymap for German MacBook Pro keyboards.

Usage

  1. Open it from Tools → Keymap Manager… or Find Action.
  2. Pick the keymap to inspect from the selector at the top; it defaults to your active one.
  3. Looking for one action? Type part of its name into the filter field beside the selector — every section then lists only the actions that match, with its count shown as "matched of total". Esc in the field, or its ✕ button, clears it.
  4. Work through the report: Keymap conflicts and Overlaps the IDE doesn't already flag (macOS takes the key), Double-bound keys (one key, several actions), Modified shortcuts (this keymap's own changes), and Inherited Shortcuts (taken from the parent as-is). Click any row for the full explanation.
  5. On a binding: Rebind… (press the new key, or click Suggest… for a free one), Remove…, Revert… to the parent's binding, or Settings… to jump to the platform Keymap page.
  6. Right-click a row in the navigator for those same operations as a context menu, without going through the detail pane first: Rebind…, Remove…, Revert… and Settings… on a shortcut row — plus Suggest a Shortcut… on a conflict, overlap or double-bound row — or, on a section row, the bulk Remove… / Revert… for that whole category. A context menu has no checkbox list to narrow things down, so it acts on every action the row names; the edit operations still open their usual dialog, where individual actions can be unticked before you apply.
  7. Use the gear menu (⚙) next to the keymap selector to Export… / Import… keymaps as XML, or to Duplicate, Rename, or Delete an editable one.
  8. Show modified only, Show Action IDs, and Show Keymap, below the report, narrow or annotate what's shown.
On a German (T1) MacBook Pro keyboard, select the bundled MacBook Pro DE keymap under Settings → Keymap to start from bindings that are actually reachable on that layout.

macOS only. Source: github.com/stefan-huettemann/keymap-manager
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.8.1 — uses only public IDE APIs, so it keeps working on 2026.2 and later.

1.8.0 — first public release.

  • Conflict report (Tools → Keymap Manager…) for any installed keymap: shortcuts macOS claims for itself, overlaps the IDE doesn't flag, and double-bound keys — each explained, with tailored advice.
  • Fix in place: rebind, remove, or revert to the parent's binding — for one action, several, or a whole category, on own and inherited bindings; also from a row's right-click menu. A read-only keymap gets an editable copy automatically.
  • The rebind field captures any key — arrows, Space, ⌫, F-keys, German keys (Ä Ö Ü ß), even IDE-bound combos like ⌃X — warns about macOS overlaps and existing bindings as you type, and can suggest a free shortcut.
  • Modified and Inherited shortcuts views, a Show modified only toggle, optional action ids and defining keymap, and a filter by action name.
  • Manage keymaps (activate, duplicate, rename, delete) and import / export them as XML.
  • Shortcuts shown as keycaps, matching Settings → Keymap; an About section in the help (?) lists what a bug report needs.
  • Bundled MacBook Pro DE keymap for the German (T1) MacBook Pro layout: the stock macOS keymap, changed only where the layout leaves a key unpressable or macOS claims the combo (58 actions).
  • Report wording adapts to the host IDE (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, Android Studio, …).

action.description: Manage keymaps and resolve shortcut conflicts with macOS and within the keymap
